description_full: UP Fintech Holding Limited provides online brokerage services focusing on Chinese investors in New Zealand, the Cayman Island, Singapore, the United States, and internationally. The company has developed a brokerage platform, Tiger Trade which allows investor to trade stocks, options, warrants, and other financial instruments that can be accessed through its APP and website. It also provides value-added services, including investor education, community engagement, and IR/PR platform services. In addition, the company offers trade execution, margin financing, and securities lending services; asset management and wealth management; ESOP management; fund license application, product design, asset custody, transaction execution, and funding allocation; fund structuring and management; and IPO underwriting services. Further, the company provides market information and simulated trading services; and trade futures contracts. UP Fintech Holding Limited was founded in 2014 and is headquartered in Singapore.

financial_summary: UP Fintech Holding Limited is a small-cap financial services business with a $745M market cap on $612M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +40% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +9.1pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 40% against a 10% cost of capital — a 30-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat.

The business throws off $1.3B in free cash flow — roughly 214 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 7.70× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage runs at 3.8×.

Shareholder yield is only 0.0%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 13% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 1.8× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
